examples/channels/18-route-static.yaml.content:
# 18 — Static routing: send to a specific agent
#
# Test:
#   1. digitorn run examples/channels/18-route-static.yaml
#   2. curl ... -d '{"question": "How do I configure my VPN?"}'
# Expected: Event routed to tech_agent (not the default main agent).

app:
  app_id: channels-18-route-static
  name: "Static Route"

modules:
  channels:
    config:
      default_agent: main
      providers:
        tech:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/tech"
          activation:
            agent: tech_agent
            message: "{{event.payload.question}}"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "General assistant. You should NOT receive tech questions."

  - id: tech_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "Technical support specialist. Answer IT and networking questions."

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/19-route-dynamic.yaml.content:
# 19 — Dynamic routing: pick agent based on event field
#
# Test:
#   1. digitorn run examples/channels/19-route-dynamic.yaml
#   2. curl ... -d '{"department": "tech", "question": "VPN issue"}'    → tech_agent
#   3. curl ... -d '{"department": "billing", "question": "Invoice"}'   → billing_agent
#   4. curl ... -d '{"department": "other", "question": "General"}'     → general_agent

app:
  app_id: channels-19-route-dynamic
  name: "Dynamic Route"

modules:
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        support:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/support"
          activation:
            route:
              field: event.payload.department
              rules:
                - match: "tech"
                  agent: tech_agent
                - match: "billing"
                  agent: billing_agent
                - default: true
                  agent: general_agent
            message: "[{{event.payload.department}}] {{event.payload.question}}"

agents:
  - id: tech_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "Technical support. Answer IT questions. Start your response with [TECH AGENT]."

  - id: billing_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "Billing support. Handle invoice and payment questions. Start with [BILLING AGENT]."

  - id: general_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "General support. Handle miscellaneous requests. Start with [GENERAL AGENT]."

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/20-prepare-enrich.yaml.content:
# 20 — Prepare step: read a file before activating the agent
#
# Test:
#   1. mkdir -p /tmp/channels-test && echo "Company: Digitorn\nPlan: Enterprise" > /tmp/channels-test/config.txt
#   2. digitorn run examples/channels/20-prepare-enrich.yaml
#   3. curl ... -d '{"user": "Alice", "question": "What plan am I on?"}'
# Expected: Agent sees the config data enriched via the prepare step.

app:
  app_id: channels-20-prepare
  name: "Prepare Enrich"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
        paths: ["/tmp/channels-test"]
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        support:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/support"
          activation:
            prepare:
              - action: filesystem.read
                params:
                  path: "/tmp/channels-test/config.txt"
                as: config_data
            context: "System config:\n{{config_data}}"
            message: "User {{event.payload.user}} asks: {{event.payload.question}}"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "Answer user questions using the system config data provided in your context."

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/21-cron-with-filesyste.content:
# 21 — Cron + filesystem: every minute, list files in a directory
#
# Test:
#   1. mkdir -p /tmp/channels-test/monitored
#   2. digitorn run examples/channels/21-cron-with-filesystem.yaml
#   3. Create files: touch /tmp/channels-test/monitored/a.txt

app:
  app_id: channels-21-cron-fs
  name: "Cron + Filesystem"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
        paths: ["/tmp/channels-test/monitored"]
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        scan:
          adapter: cron
          config:
            schedule: "* * * * *"
          activation:
            message: "List all files in /tmp/channels-test/monitored/ and report the count."

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are a directory monitor. Use filesystem.ls to list the directory
      and report how many files are present.

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/22-cron-write-report.y.content:
# 22 — Cron: generate a report file every 2 minutes
#
# Test:
#   1. mkdir -p /tmp/channels-test/reports
#   2. digitorn run examples/channels/22-cron-write-report.yaml
# Expected: Every 2 minutes, a new report file appears in /tmp/channels-test/reports/

app:

modules:

          adapter: cron

agents:

      Write it using filesystem.write to /tmp/channels-test/reports/ with a unique filename.

  mode: background

examples/channels/23-webhook-to-log.yaml.content:
# 23 — Webhook inbound → agent processes → sends to log output
#
# Test:
#   1. digitorn run examples/channels/23-webhook-to-log.yaml
#   2. curl ... -d '{"event": "user_signup", "user": "alice@example.com"}'
# Expected: Agent processes the event and sends a formatted log entry.

app:
  app_id: channels-23-webhook-log
  name: "Webhook to Log"

modules:
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        events:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/events"
          activation:
            message: "Process this event and send a formatted log to the 'audit' channel: {{event.payload.event}} by {{event.payload.user}}"

        audit:
          adapter: log
          config:
            level: info
            logger: "digitorn.audit"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are an audit agent. Process incoming events and send a formatted
      audit log entry to the "audit" channel using:
      channels.send_message(provider="audit", text="[AUDIT] ...")

execution:
  mode: background

capabilities:
  grant:
    - module: channels
      actions: [send_message]
      reason: "Send formatted audit log entries to the audit channel"

examples/channels/24-multi-provider-send.content:
# 24 — Agent sends to multiple outbound providers
#
# Test:
#   1. digitorn run examples/channels/24-multi-provider-send.yaml
#   2. curl ... -d '{"alert": "CPU > 90%", "severity": "high"}'
# Expected: Agent sends to both log_debug and log_alerts.

app:
  app_id: channels-24-multi-send
  name: "Multi Provider Send"

modules:
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        inbound:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/alerts"
          activation:
            message: "Alert: {{event.payload.alert}} (severity: {{event.payload.severity}}). Broadcast to all output channels."

        log_debug:
          adapter: log
          config:
            level: debug
            logger: "digitorn.debug"

        log_alerts:
          adapter: log
          config:
            level: warning
            logger: "digitorn.alerts"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      When you receive an alert, broadcast it to all output channels:
      1. channels.send_message(provider="log_debug", text="[DEBUG] ...")
      2. channels.send_message(provider="log_alerts", text="[ALERT] ...")

execution:
  mode: background

capabilities:
  grant:
    - module: channels
      actions: [send_message]
      reason: "Send alert messages to individual output channels"
    - module: channels
      actions: [broadcast]
      reason: "Broadcast alerts to multiple channels simultaneously"
    - module: channels
      actions: [list_providers]
      reason: "Discover available channel providers"

examples/channels/25-broadcast.yaml.content:
# 25 — Broadcast: send same message to multiple providers at once
#
# Test:

modules:

          adapter: log
          config:
            level: info
            logger: "digitorn.channel_a"

          adapter: log
          config:
            level: info
            logger: "digitorn.channel_b"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:

capabilities:

      reason: "Broadcast status messages to multiple log channels at once"
    - module: channels
      actions: [list_providers]

examples/channels/26-cron-db-check.yaml.content:

agents:

        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"

  mode: background

examples/channels/27-prepare-db-lookup.y.content:
# 27 — Prepare: DB lookup before agent activation
#
# Test:
#   1. sqlite3 /tmp/channels-test/test.db "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients(id INTEGER, name TEXT, plan TEXT); INSERT OR REPLACE INTO clients VALUES(1,'Alice','premium'),(2,'Bob','free');"
#   2. digitorn run examples/channels/27-prepare-db-lookup.yaml
#   3. curl ... -d '{"client_id": 1, "question": "What features do I have?"}'
# Expected: Agent sees client data from the prepare step.

app:
  app_id: channels-27-prepare-db
  name: "Prepare DB Lookup"

modules:
  database:
    setup:
        - action: connect
          params:
            connection_id: test_db
            driver: sqlite
            url: "sqlite:///tmp/channels-test/test.db"
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        support:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/support"
          activation:
            prepare:
              - action: database.fetch_results
                params:
                  query: "SELECT name, plan FROM clients WHERE id = {{event.payload.client_id}}"
                as: client
            context: "Client: {{client}}"
            message: "{{event.payload.question}}"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "Answer the client's question using their account info from context."

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/28-file-watcher-read-p.content:
# 28 — File watcher: detect new JSON file, read it, process, write result
#
# Test:
#   1. mkdir -p /tmp/channels-test/json-inbox /tmp/channels-test/json-output
#   2. digitorn run examples/channels/28-file-watcher-read-process.yaml
#   3. echo '{"items": [{"name": "Widget", "price": 10}, {"name": "Gadget", "price": 25}]}' > /tmp/channels-test/json-inbox/order.json
# Expected: Agent reads the JSON, calculates total, writes a summary file.

app:
  app_id: channels-28-json-process
  name: "JSON File Processor"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
        paths: ["/tmp/channels-test/json-inbox", "/tmp/channels-test/json-output"]
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        json_inbox:
          adapter: file_watcher
          config:
            paths: ["/tmp/channels-test/json-inbox/*.json"]
            poll_interval: 3
          activation:
            message: |
              New JSON file: {{event.payload.path}}
              1. Read it with filesystem.read
              2. Parse and analyze the data
              3. Write a summary to /tmp/channels-test/json-output/summary-{{event.payload.filename}}.txt

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are a file processor. Read JSON files, analyze their contents,
      calculate totals, and write summary reports.

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/29-multi-filter.yaml.content:
# 29 — Multiple filters (AND logic): status=new AND priority < 3
#
# Test:
#   1. digitorn run examples/channels/29-multi-filter.yaml
#   2. curl ... -d '{"status": "new", "priority": 1, "title": "Critical bug"}'     → processed
#   3. curl ... -d '{"status": "new", "priority": 5, "title": "Low prio"}'         → dropped (priority)
#   4. curl ... -d '{"status": "closed", "priority": 1, "title": "Already done"}'  → dropped (status)

app:
  app_id: channels-29-multi-filter
  name: "Multi Filter AND"

modules:
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        tickets:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/tickets"
          activation:
            filter:
              - field: event.payload.status
                equals: "new"
              - field: event.payload.priority
                lt: 3
            message: "High-priority new ticket: {{event.payload.title}} (P{{event.payload.priority}})"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "Handle critical new tickets only. Acknowledge and suggest immediate resolution steps."

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/30-route-with-prepare..content:
# 30 — Prepare + route combined: lookup client, route by plan
#
# Test:
#   1. sqlite3 /tmp/channels-test/test.db "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients(id INTEGER, name TEXT, plan TEXT); INSERT OR REPLACE INTO clients VALUES(1,'Alice','premium'),(2,'Bob','free');"
#   2. digitorn run examples/channels/30-route-with-prepare.yaml
#   3. curl ... -d '{"client_id": 1, "message": "Help me"}'  → vip_agent (premium)
#   4. curl ... -d '{"client_id": 2, "message": "Help me"}'  → standard_agent (free)

app:
  app_id: channels-30-prepare-route
  name: "Prepare + Route"

modules:
  database:
    setup:
        - action: connect
          params:
            connection_id: test_db
            driver: sqlite
            url: "sqlite:///tmp/channels-test/test.db"
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        support:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/support"
          activation:
            prepare:
              - action: database.fetch_results
                params:
                  query: "SELECT name, plan FROM clients WHERE id = {{event.payload.client_id}}"
                as: client
            route:
              field: client.0.plan
              rules:
                - match: "premium"
                  agent: vip_agent
                - default: true
                  agent: standard_agent
            context: "Client: {{client}}"
            message: "{{event.payload.message}}"

agents:
  - id: vip_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "VIP support. Start your response with [VIP AGENT]. Provide premium service."

  - id: standard_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "Standard support. Start your response with [STANDARD AGENT]."

execution:
  mode: background

examples/channels/31-cron-capabilities.y.content:

agents:

examples/channels/33-full-pipeline.yaml.content:
# 33 — Full pipeline: filter + prepare + route + context + reply:auto
#
# This tests the complete activation pipeline end-to-end.
#
# Test:
#   1. sqlite3 /tmp/channels-test/test.db "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients(id INTEGER, name TEXT, plan TEXT, dept TEXT); INSERT OR REPLACE INTO clients VALUES(1,'Alice','premium','tech'),(2,'Bob','free','billing'),(3,'Charlie','premium','billing');"
#   2. digitorn run examples/channels/33-full-pipeline.yaml
#   3. curl ... -d '{"client_id": 1, "status": "new", "message": "VPN not working"}'
#      → filter passes (new), prepare lookups Alice (premium, tech), route → tech_agent
#   4. curl ... -d '{"client_id": 2, "status": "closed", "message": "Old"}'
#      → filter drops (not new)
#   5. curl ... -d '{"client_id": 3, "status": "new", "message": "Invoice wrong"}'
#      → filter passes, prepare lookups Charlie (premium, billing), route → billing_agent

app:
  app_id: channels-33-full-pipeline
  name: "Full Pipeline"

modules:
  database:
    setup:
        - action: connect
          params:
            connection_id: test_db
            driver: sqlite
            url: "sqlite:///tmp/channels-test/test.db"
  channels:
    config:
      providers:
        tickets:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/tickets"
          activation:
            filter:
              - field: event.payload.status
                equals: "new"
            prepare:
              - action: database.fetch_results
                params:
                  query: "SELECT name, plan, dept FROM clients WHERE id = {{event.payload.client_id}}"
                as: client
            route:
              field: client.0.dept
              rules:
                - match: "tech"
                  agent: tech_agent
                - match: "billing"
                  agent: billing_agent
                - default: true
                  agent: general_agent
            context: |
              Client: {{client.0.name}} (plan: {{client.0.plan}}, dept: {{client.0.dept}})
            message: "{{event.payload.message}}"
            session: "ticket-{{event.payload.client_id}}"

        audit:
          adapter: log
          config:
            level: info
            logger: "digitorn.audit"

agents:
  - id: tech_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      Technical support agent. Start with [TECH]. Use the client context.
      After resolving, log to the audit channel.

  - id: billing_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      Billing support agent. Start with [BILLING]. Use the client context.

  - id: general_agent
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: "General support. Start with [GENERAL]."

execution:
  mode: background

capabilities:
  grant:
    - module: channels
      actions: [send_message]
      reason: "Send audit log entries after processing support tickets"
    - module: channels
      actions: [list_providers]
      reason: "Discover available channel providers"

examples/channels/34-monitoring-station..content:
# 34 — Monitoring station: cron checks + file watch + webhook alerts
#
# A real-world monitoring app that:
# - Runs health checks every minute (cron)
# - Watches for config file changes (file_watcher)
# - Receives external alerts via webhook
# - Sends notifications to log
# - Uses filesystem + database for state
#
# Test:
#   1. mkdir -p /tmp/channels-test/monitoring /tmp/channels-test/config
#   2. sqlite3 /tmp/channels-test/monitoring.db "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS checks(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, timestamp TEXT, status TEXT, details TEXT);"
#   3. digitorn run examples/channels/34-monitoring-station.yaml
#   4. Wait for cron ticks
#   5. echo "debug=true" > /tmp/channels-test/config/app.conf
#   6. curl ... -d '{"source": "prometheus", "alert": "HighCPU", "severity": "warning"}'

app:
  app_id: channels-34-monitoring
  name: "Monitoring Station"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
        paths: ["/tmp/channels-test/monitoring", "/tmp/channels-test/config"]
  database:
    setup:
        - action: connect
          params:
            connection_id: monitoring_db
            driver: sqlite
            url: "sqlite:///tmp/channels-test/monitoring.db"
  memory: {}
  channels:
    config:
      default_agent: monitor
      max_turns: 15
      timeout: 60
      providers:
        health_check:
          adapter: cron
          config:
            schedule: "* * * * *"
          activation:
            message: |
              Run a health check:
              1. Check if /tmp/channels-test/monitoring/ directory is accessible (filesystem.ls)
              2. Insert a check record into the database
              3. Send a status summary to the "alerts" channel

        config_watcher:
          adapter: file_watcher
          config:
            paths: ["/tmp/channels-test/config/*"]
            poll_interval: 5
          activation:
            message: |
              Config file changed: {{event.payload.filename}}
              1. Read the file content
              2. Report what changed
              3. Log it to the "alerts" channel

        external_alerts:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/alerts"
          activation:
            filter:
              - field: event.payload.severity
                not_equals: "info"
            context: "External alert from {{event.payload.source}}: {{event.payload.alert}}"
            message: "Handle this alert: {{event.payload.alert}} (severity: {{event.payload.severity}})"

        alerts:
          adapter: log
          config:
            level: warning
            logger: "digitorn.monitoring.alerts"

agents:
  - id: monitor
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are an infrastructure monitoring agent. You:
      - Run periodic health checks and record results in the database
      - Watch for config file changes and report them
      - Handle external alerts from monitoring systems
      - Send important notifications to the "alerts" channel

      Always use channels.send_message(provider="alerts", text="...") for notifications.

execution:
  mode: background

capabilities:
  grant:
    - module: channels
      actions: [send_message]
      reason: "Send health check and alert notifications to the alerts channel"
    - module: channels
      actions: [list_providers]
      reason: "Discover available channel providers"
    - module: channels
      actions: [stats]
      reason: "Read channel delivery statistics for monitoring reports"

examples/channels/35-it-support-center.y.content:
# 35 — IT Support Center: the ultimate integration test
#
# Full-featured app combining ALL channels features:
# - 4 inbound providers (cron, file_watcher, 2x webhook)
# - 1 outbound provider (log)
# - Filters, prepare steps, dynamic routing
# - Shared sessions, context injection
# - Multiple specialized agents
# - Database, filesystem, memory modules
# - Capability restrictions
#
# Test:
#   1. Setup:
#      mkdir -p /tmp/channels-test/support-docs /tmp/channels-test/uploads
#      sqlite3 /tmp/channels-test/support.db "
#        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS clients(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT, email TEXT, plan TEXT, department TEXT);
#        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tickets(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, client_id INTEGER, title TEXT, status TEXT, created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP);
#        INSERT OR REPLACE INTO clients VALUES(1,'Alice Martin','alice@corp.com','premium','engineering');
#        INSERT OR REPLACE INTO clients VALUES(2,'Bob Dupont','bob@corp.com','free','marketing');
#        INSERT OR REPLACE INTO clients VALUES(3,'Charlie Roux','charlie@corp.com','premium','finance');
#        INSERT INTO tickets(client_id,title,status) VALUES(1,'VPN Issue','open'),(1,'Laptop slow','resolved'),(3,'Excel crash','open');
#      "
#      echo "VPN: Check certificate expiry. Reinstall if expired.\nEmail: Verify SMTP settings.\nPrinter: Restart spooler service." > /tmp/channels-test/support-docs/procedures.txt
#
#   2. Run: digitorn run examples/channels/35-it-support-center.yaml
#
#   3. Test cron: wait 1 minute → agent runs daily check
#
#   4. Test file upload: echo "error log data" > /tmp/channels-test/uploads/crash.log
#
#   5. Test support ticket (webhook):
#      curl -X POST http://localhost:PORT/hook/support -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
#        -d '{"client_id": 1, "status": "new", "category": "network", "message": "VPN not connecting since this morning"}'
#
#   6. Test external alert (webhook):
#      curl -X POST http://localhost:PORT/hook/monitoring -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
#        -d '{"source": "nagios", "alert": "Server01 CPU 95%", "severity": "critical"}'

app:
  app_id: channels-35-support
  name: "IT Support Center"
  description: "Multi-channel IT support with routing, enrichment, and specialized agents"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
        paths: ["/tmp/channels-test/support-docs", "/tmp/channels-test/uploads"]

  database:
    setup:
        - action: connect
          params:
            connection_id: support_db
            driver: sqlite
            url: "sqlite:///tmp/channels-test/support.db"

  memory: {}

  channels:
    config:
      default_agent: receptionist
      max_turns: 20
      timeout: 90
      secret_filter_enabled: true
      providers:
        # ── Periodic health check (cron) ──
        daily_check:
          adapter: cron
          config:
            schedule: "* * * * *"
          activation:
            agent: monitor
            message: |
              Daily check:
              1. Query the database for open tickets: SELECT id, title, status, created_at FROM tickets WHERE status='open'
              2. Report how many open tickets exist
              3. Send a summary to the "notifications" channel

        # ── File upload watcher ──
        upload_watcher:
          adapter: file_watcher
          config:
            paths: ["/tmp/channels-test/uploads/*"]
            poll_interval: 5
          activation:
            agent: file_analyst
            message: "New upload: {{event.payload.filename}} ({{event.payload.size}} bytes). Read and analyze the file."

        # ── Support tickets (webhook with full pipeline) ──
        support_tickets:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/support"
          activation:
            filter:
              - field: event.payload.status
                equals: "new"
            prepare:
              - action: database.fetch_results
                params:
                  query: "SELECT name, email, plan, department FROM clients WHERE id = {{event.payload.client_id}}"
                as: client
              - action: database.fetch_results
                params:
                  query: "SELECT id, title, status FROM tickets WHERE client_id = {{event.payload.client_id}} AND status = 'open'"
                as: open_tickets
              - action: filesystem.read
                params:
                  path: "/tmp/channels-test/support-docs/procedures.txt"
                as: procedures
            route:
              field: event.payload.category
              rules:
                - match: "network"
                  agent: network_expert
                - match: "software"
                  agent: software_expert
                - default: true
                  agent: receptionist
            session: "ticket-{{event.payload.client_id}}"
            context: |
              Client: {{client.0.name}} ({{client.0.email}})
              Plan: {{client.0.plan}} | Department: {{client.0.department}}
              Open tickets: {{open_tickets}}
              IT Procedures: {{procedures}}
            message: "{{event.payload.message}}"

        # ── External monitoring alerts (webhook) ──
        monitoring:
          adapter: webhook
          config:
            inbound_path: "/hook/monitoring"
          activation:
            filter:
              - field: event.payload.severity
                not_equals: "info"
            agent: monitor
            context: "ALERT from {{event.payload.source}}: {{event.payload.alert}} ({{event.payload.severity}})"
            message: "Handle this alert immediately: {{event.payload.alert}}"

        # ── Notification output (log) ──
        notifications:
          adapter: log
          config:
            level: warning
            logger: "digitorn.support.notifications"

agents:
  - id: receptionist
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are the IT support receptionist. Start your responses with [RECEPTIONIST].
      - Greet the client by name (from context)
      - Assess the issue based on their message and open tickets
      - If the client is premium, prioritize their request
      - For simple issues, resolve directly using the procedures
      - For complex issues, acknowledge and explain next steps
      - Send important updates to the "notifications" channel

  - id: network_expert
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are the network specialist. Start responses with [NETWORK].
      - Diagnose VPN, DNS, firewall, and connectivity issues
      - Reference the IT procedures from context
      - Check client's open tickets for related issues
      - Insert a new ticket record in the database when needed
      - Send resolution to "notifications"

  - id: software_expert
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are the software specialist. Start responses with [SOFTWARE].
      - Handle software installation, configuration, and crash issues
      - Check client's history for recurring problems

  - id: monitor
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are the monitoring agent. Start responses with [MONITOR].
      - For daily checks: query the database and report ticket stats
      - For alerts: assess severity and suggest remediation
      - Always send summaries to the "notifications" channel

  - id: file_analyst
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      You are the file analyst. Start responses with [FILE].
      - Read uploaded files using filesystem.read
      - Analyze content (logs, reports, data)
      - Report findings

execution:
  mode: background

capabilities:
  grant:
    - module: channels
      actions: [send_message]
      reason: "Send ticket updates and alerts to the notifications channel"
    - module: channels
      actions: [list_providers]
      reason: "Discover available channel providers"
    - module: channels
      actions: [stats]
      reason: "Read channel delivery statistics for monitoring reports"
    - module: channels
      actions: [provider_history]
      reason: "Access provider message history for audit and diagnostics"

# 36 — Live Gmail test: IMAP inbound + SMTP outbound
#
# Setup:
#   1. Enable IMAP in Gmail: Settings > Forwarding and POP/IMAP > Enable IMAP
#   2. Create an App Password: https://myaccount.google.com/apppasswords
#      (requires 2FA enabled on the Google account)
#   3. Export credentials:
#      export GMAIL_ADDRESS="your.email@gmail.com"
#      export GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD="xxxx xxxx xxxx xxxx"
#
# Test:
#   digitorn run examples/channels/36-gmail-live.yaml
#
#   Then send an email to your Gmail address.
#   The agent reads the email, processes it, and replies automatically.
#
# Expected:
#   - IMAP polls every 30s for new (UNSEEN) emails
#   - Agent receives the email body as user message
#   - Agent reply is sent back via SMTP to the sender

app:
  app_id: channels-36-gmail
  name: "Gmail Live Test"

modules:
  channels:
    config:
      default_agent: main
      max_turns: 10
      timeout: 60
      providers:
        gmail_inbox:
          adapter: email
          config:
            imap:
              host: imap.gmail.com
              port: 993
              user: "{{env.GMAIL_ADDRESS}}"
              password: "{{secret.GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD}}"
              folder: INBOX
            smtp:
              host: smtp.gmail.com
              port: 587
              user: "{{env.GMAIL_ADDRESS}}"
              password: "{{secret.GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD}}"
            from_address: "{{env.GMAIL_ADDRESS}}"
            poll_interval: 30
          activation:
            message: |
              New email from {{event.payload.from}}:
              Subject: {{event.payload.subject}}

              {{event.payload.body}}
            context: |
              You received this email at {{event.timestamp}}.
              Reply concisely and helpfully. Sign as "Digitorn Assistant".
            reply: auto
            session: "email-{{event.payload.from}}"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      model: deepseek-chat
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
    role: |
      Tu es un assistant email intelligent. Tu reponds aux emails de maniere
      concise, professionnelle et utile. Tu signes "Digitorn Assistant".

  mode: background

# 38 — Channels + MCP: cron trigger + MCP filesystem server

#
# Setup:
#   mkdir -p /tmp/digitorn-mcp-test

app:

modules:

agents:

examples/opencode/app.yaml.content:
# OpenCode — Claude Code equivalent
#
# Same tools, same workflow, same philosophy:
#   Read, Write, Edit, Glob/Find, Grep, Bash + Memory + Sub-agents
#
# Usage:
#   digitorn run examples/opencode/app.yaml
#   digitorn run examples/opencode/app.yaml --standalone

app:
  app_id: opencode
  name: "OpenCode"
  version: "4.0"
  description: "Terminal coding assistant — Claude Code equivalent"

modules:
  filesystem: {}

  shell: {}

  lsp:
    config:
      python: "ruff check --output-format=json"

  memory:
    config:
      working_memory: true
      todo_list: true
      runtime:
        goal_guardian: true

  web:
    config:
      search:
        primary: duckduckgo

skills:
  - command: "/commit"
    description: "Smart git commit"
    path: "./skills/commit.md"
  - command: "/review"
    description: "Code review"
    path: "./skills/review.md"
  - command: "/pr"
    description: "Create pull request"
    path: "./skills/pr.md"
  - command: "/test"
    description: "Detect and run tests"
    path: "./skills/test.md"
  - command: "/init"
    description: "Detect project stack"
    path: "./skills/init.md"
  - command: "/debug"
    description: "Systematic debugging"
    path: "./skills/debug.md"

agents:
  - id: main
    role: coordinator
    brain:
      provider: minimax
      model: MiniMax-M2.5
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.MINIMAX_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.minimaxi.chat/v1"
      temperature: 0.1
      max_tokens: 4096
      context:
        max_tokens: 800000
        strategy: summarize
        keep_recent: 6
        auto_compact: true
    plan_first: false
    system_prompt: |
      You are an interactive agent that helps users with software engineering tasks. Use the tools available to you to assist the user.

      Workspace: {WORKSPACE}

      # System

      - All text you output is displayed to the user. Output text to communicate.
      - You can call multiple tools in a single response. Make all independent tool calls in parallel.
      - If tool calls depend on each other, call them sequentially — do NOT guess missing parameters.

      # Planning — THINK BEFORE YOU CODE

      For ANY task that is not a simple question or single-file fix, you MUST plan first.

      ## Simple tasks (no plan needed)
      - "What does this function do?" → just read and answer
      - "Fix this typo" → just edit
      - "Run the tests" → just bash

      ## Non-trivial tasks (PLAN REQUIRED)
      Any task involving 2+ files, architecture decisions, or multi-step work:

      **Step 1 — Research** (do NOT write code yet)
      - Read the relevant files to understand current state
      - If broad search needed → spawn explore agents in parallel
      - For complex architecture → spawn_agent(specialist="plan", task="Analyze X and design implementation plan for Y")
      - Understand the existing patterns, conventions, dependencies

      **Step 2 — Plan** (present to user BEFORE coding)
      - set_goal("what you need to accomplish")
      - Write a clear plan as text output to the user:
        - What files will be created/modified
        - The approach and why
        - What won't be changed
        - Risks or trade-offs
      - add_todo() for each step of the plan
      - WAIT for user confirmation before proceeding

      **Step 3 — Execute** (only after user says yes/ok/go/oui)
      - update_todo(id, "in_progress") before each step
      - Do the work
      - update_todo(id, "done") after each step
      - remember("key finding") for important discoveries

      **Step 4 — Verify**
      - Run tests if applicable
      - Read modified files to confirm correctness
      - Report what was done

      NEVER skip the plan for non-trivial tasks. If you're about to modify 2+ files without having shown a plan, STOP and plan first.

      After context compaction, check your memory above before continuing.

      # Using your tools

      Use the RIGHT tool for the job. Do NOT use bash when a dedicated tool exists:
        - To read files → read (not bash cat/head/tail)
        - To edit files → edit (not bash sed/awk)
        - To create files → write (not bash echo)
        - To search content → grep (not bash grep/rg)
        - To find files → glob (not bash find)
      Use bash for: listing directories, git, build tools, test runners, package managers, system commands.

      You can call multiple tools in parallel when they are independent.

      # Reading code

      - grep(pattern, path) is your primary search tool. Always grep first, then read the matching lines.
      - glob(pattern) to find files by pattern. Supports '*.py', '**/*.tsx', 'src/**/*.ts'.
      - read(path) with start_line/end_line for specific sections. Never read entire large files.
      - read(path, pattern="search term") to search within a file and get matching lines with context.

      # Editing code — SURGICAL EDITS ONLY

      NEVER rewrite entire files. Always use surgical edits:
      - edit(path, old_string, new_string) — find and replace exact text. The old_string must be unique in the file.
      - edit(path, old_string, new_string, replace_all=true) — replace all occurrences (for renames).
      - write(path, content) — ONLY for creating brand new files.
      - After each edit, verify by reading the changed section.
      - If edit fails (old_string not found), re-read the file — content may have changed.

      # Shell

      - bash(command) for one-off commands. CWD persists between calls.
      - bash_background(command) for dev servers and long-running processes. Returns a task_id.
      - bash_status(task_id) to check output of background tasks, or kill them with kill=true.

      # Sub-agents — MANDATORY for broad searches

      When you need to search across many files or explore a codebase:
      - spawn_agent(specialist="explore", task="Find all X in Y")
      - For 2+ independent research questions → spawn MULTIPLE explore agents in PARALLEL
      - Collect results with agent_wait_all() and synthesize
      Do NOT do sequential grep-grep-grep when you could delegate to explore agents in parallel.
      Do NOT spawn agents for simple single-file reads — use read() directly.

      # Git

      - Always git status before and after changes.
      - Never push unless user explicitly asks.
      - Never amend commits unless asked. Always create new commits.
      - Stage specific files, never git add -A or git add .
      - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or force push.

      # Rules

      - Read code before modifying it. Do not propose changes to code you haven't read.
      - Prefer editing existing files over creating new ones.
      - Do NOT over-engineer: no extra features, no unnecessary abstractions, no docstrings on unchanged code.
      - Be careful with security: no command injection, XSS, SQL injection.
      - For destructive actions (delete, git reset, force push) — ask the user first.
      - After 3 failed attempts at the same thing, stop and explain.
      - Do NOT narrate tool calls. Don't say "Let me read..." — just call the tool.
      - Be concise. Lead with the answer, not the reasoning.
    pool:
      max_workers: 3

  - id: explore
    role: specialist
    specialty: "Fast codebase exploration. Read-only."
    brain:
      provider: minimax
      model: MiniMax-M2.5
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.MINIMAX_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.minimaxi.chat/v1"
      temperature: 0.0
      max_tokens: 2048
    system_prompt: |
      You are a fast codebase explorer. Find information quickly in as few tool calls as possible.

      How to search:
      - grep(pattern, path) for definitions, imports, usages
      - find(pattern) for files by name
      - read(path, start_line, end_line) for specific sections — never entire large files

      Return:
      - File paths with line numbers (file.py:42)
      - Short excerpts (relevant lines only)
      - Match count
      - Be concise. Facts, not commentary.

      Never modify files. Never run shell commands.
    modules: [filesystem, memory]

  - id: plan
    role: specialist
    specialty: "Architecture and implementation planning. Read-only."
    brain:
      provider: minimax
      model: MiniMax-M2.5
      backend: openai_compat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.MINIMAX_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.minimaxi.chat/v1"
      temperature: 0.1
      max_tokens: 4096
    system_prompt: |
      You are a software architect agent. Your job is to analyze a codebase and design an implementation plan.

      Process:
      1. Read the relevant files to understand current architecture
      2. Identify patterns, conventions, and dependencies
      3. Design a step-by-step implementation plan

      Your plan must include:
      - Which files to create or modify (with exact paths)
      - The approach and why it fits the existing patterns
      - What NOT to change (boundaries)
      - Risks or trade-offs
      - Ordered steps from first to last

      Rules:
      - Never modify files. Read-only.
      - Be specific: name exact files, functions, line ranges.
      - Consider existing conventions — don't fight the codebase.
      - Keep the plan minimal — only what's needed, nothing extra.
      - If you see multiple approaches, pick one and explain why.
    modules: [filesystem, memory]

execution:
  mode: conversation
  workspace_mode: required
  greeting: |
    Ready. What are we working on?
  workspace: ""
  project_memory: auto
  max_turns: 200
  timeout: 1800
  hooks:
    - id: lint_after_edit
      on: tool_end
      condition:
        type: tool_match
        tools: ["filesystem.edit", "filesystem.write"]
      action:
        type: module_action
        name: lsp.notify_change
        action_params:
          path: "{{tool.params.path}}"
      cooldown: 2

capabilities:
  default_policy: block
  max_risk_level: medium
  grant:
    - module: filesystem
      actions: [read, write, edit, grep, glob]
    - module: shell
      actions: [bash, bash_background, bash_status]
    - module: memory
      actions: [set_goal, remember, recall, forget, add_todo, update_todo]
    - module: web
      actions: [search, fetch, extract, download]
    - module: agent_spawn
      actions: [agent]

# 25 — Ingestion de lignes de base de données
# Indexe le contenu des tables avec templates personnalisés.
# Sync automatique via updated_at.

app:
  app_id: rag-25-db-rows
  name: "RAG Database Rows"

modules:
  database:
    setup:
      - action: connect
        params:
          connection_id: crm
          driver: sqlite
          database: "/tmp/rag-real-test/crm.db"
          policy:
            preset: readonly

  rag:
    sources:
      - type: database
        connection_id: crm
        sync:
          strategy: updated_at
          interval: 30
        tables:
          customers:
            columns: [id, name, email, company, segment, notes]
            mode: embed_rows
            template: "Client: {name} ({company}, segment {segment}) - {email} - Notes: {notes}"
            max_rows: 10000
          products:
            columns: [id, name, description, price, category]
            mode: embed_rows

modules:

      confidence_threshold: 0.5
      fallback: broader_query
    pipeline:
      retrieval: hybrid
      rerank_top_n: 20
      final_top_k: 5
    citations:

      verify: true

  llm_provider:

        config:
          api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"

agents:

examples/rag/28-full-pipeline.yaml.content:
# 28 — Pipeline RAG complet
# Hybrid + reranker + multi-query + CRAG + cache + citations vérifiées.
# La configuration la plus complète sans base de données.

app:
  app_id: rag-28-full-pipeline
  name: "RAG Full Pipeline"

variables:
  workspace: "{{env.PWD}}"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
      paths: ["{{workspace}}"]
      allowed_actions: [read, glob, grep]
  rag:
    embedding_model: bge-m3
    reranker: bge-reranker-v2
    backend:
      type: qdrant
      path: "/tmp/digitorn-full-rag"
      quantization: int8
    pipeline:
      retrieval: hybrid
      bm25_weight: 0.3
      semantic_weight: 0.7
      multi_query:
        enabled: true
        provider: helper
        num_variants: 3
      rerank_top_n: 30
      final_top_k: 5
    chunking:
      strategy: recursive
      size: 600
      overlap: 80
    sources:
      - type: file
        path: "{{workspace}}/knowledge"
        extensions: [.md, .txt, .pdf, .html]
        watch: true
        recursive: true
    auto_index:
      on_start: true
    cache:
      enabled: true
      similarity_threshold: 0.92
      ttl: 3600
      max_entries: 20000
    citations:
      enabled: true
      format: inline
      verify: true
    crag:
      enabled: true
      provider: helper
      confidence_threshold: 0.4
      fallback: broader_query

  llm_provider:
    providers:
      helper:
        backend: openai_compat
        model: deepseek-chat
        config:
          api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
          base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      backend: openai_compat
      model: deepseek-chat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      temperature: 0.2
      context:
        max_tokens: 128000
        strategy: summarize
        keep_recent: 10
    system_prompt: |
      Tu es un assistant de recherche expert avec le pipeline RAG le plus avancé :
      - Embeddings BGE-M3 multilingues (100+ langues)
      - Recherche hybride (sémantique + BM25)
      - Expansion multi-query (3 variantes)
      - Reranking cross-encoder BGE-v2
      - Corrective RAG (fallback automatique)
      - Cache sémantique
      - Citations vérifiées

      Réponds toujours avec des citations [N]. Sois précis et exhaustif.

execution:
  mode: conversation
  workspace: "{{workspace}}"
  greeting: |
    Pipeline RAG complet activé :
    BGE-M3 + hybrid + multi-query + reranker + CRAG + cache + citations.

# 29 — Enterprise multi-source (docs + DB + Text2SQL)
# Combine fichiers, base de données, et Text2SQL.
# Le routeur adaptatif choisit automatiquement la meilleure stratégie.

app:
  app_id: rag-29-enterprise
  name: "Enterprise RAG Multi-Source"

variables:
  workspace: "{{env.PWD}}"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
      paths: ["{{workspace}}"]
      allowed_actions: [read, glob, grep]
  spreadsheet: {}
  database:
    setup:
      - action: connect
        params:
          connection_id: main_db
          driver: sqlite
          database: "{{workspace}}/enterprise.db"
          policy:
            preset: readonly

  rag:
    embedding_model: bge-m3
    reranker: true
    backend:
      type: qdrant
      path: "/tmp/digitorn-enterprise"
      quantization: int8
    pipeline:
      retrieval: hybrid
      multi_query:
        enabled: true
        provider: helper
        num_variants: 3
      rerank_top_n: 25
      final_top_k: 5
    sources:
      - type: file
        path: "{{workspace}}/docs"
        extensions: [.md, .txt, .pdf]
        watch: true
        recursive: true
      - type: file
        path: "{{workspace}}/reports"
        extensions: [.pdf, .xlsx]
        watch: true
      - type: database
        connection_id: main_db
        sync:
          strategy: updated_at
          interval: 60
        tables:
          employees:
            columns: [id, name, department, role, skills]
            mode: embed_rows
            template: "{name} — {role} ({department}) — Compétences: {skills}"
          projects:
            columns: [id, name, description, status, lead]
            mode: embed_rows
            template: "Projet: {name} ({status}) — {description} — Responsable: {lead}"
          clients:
            columns: [id, company, contact, sector]
            mode: embed_rows
            template: "Client: {company} ({sector}) — Contact: {contact}"
          invoices:
            mode: schema_only
          timesheets:
            mode: schema_only
    auto_index:
      on_start: true
    cache:
      enabled: true
      ttl: 1800
    citations:
      enabled: true
      verify: true
    text2sql:
      enabled: true
      provider: helper
      example_cache: true

  llm_provider:
    providers:
      helper:
        backend: openai_compat
        model: deepseek-chat
        config:
          api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
          base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"

agents:
  - id: main
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      backend: openai_compat
      model: deepseek-chat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      temperature: 0.2
      context:
        max_tokens: 128000
        strategy: summarize
        keep_recent: 10
    system_prompt: |
      Tu es l'assistant enterprise avec accès à toutes les sources :

      **Documents** : docs techniques, rapports PDF et Excel
      **Base de données** : employés, projets, clients (recherche sémantique)
      **Analytique** : factures, feuilles de temps (Text2SQL)

      Stratégie :
      - Questions sur les personnes/projets/clients → rag.query
      - Questions analytiques (combien, total, moyenne) → rag.sql_query
      - Questions complexes → rag.multi_query

      Cite TOUJOURS tes sources avec [N].

execution:
  mode: conversation
  workspace: "{{workspace}}"
  greeting: |
    Enterprise RAG multi-source prêt :
    - Documentation (MD, PDF, Excel)
    - Données CRM (employés, projets, clients)
    - Analytique SQL (factures, timesheets)

    Posez votre question.

examples/rag/30-ultimate-multiagent.yaml.content:
# 30 — Ultimate : multi-agent RAG avec spécialistes
# Un coordinateur route vers des agents spécialisés :
# - Chercheur : RAG hybride + multi-query + CRAG
# - Analyste : Text2SQL + données structurées
# - Rédacteur : synthèse avec citations vérifiées
# Tous partagent les mêmes knowledge bases.

app:
  app_id: rag-30-ultimate
  name: "Ultimate Multi-Agent RAG"

variables:
  workspace: "{{env.PWD}}"

modules:
  filesystem:
    constraints:
      paths: ["{{workspace}}"]
      allowed_actions: [read, glob, grep, write]
  spreadsheet: {}
  memory:
    config:
      working_memory: true
      todo_list: true
  database:
    setup:
      - action: connect
        params:
          connection_id: main_db
          driver: sqlite
          database: "{{workspace}}/data.db"
          policy:
            preset: readonly

  rag:
    embedding_model: bge-m3
    reranker: bge-reranker-v2
    backend:
      type: qdrant
      path: "/tmp/digitorn-ultimate"
      quantization: int8
    pipeline:
      retrieval: hybrid
      bm25_weight: 0.3
      semantic_weight: 0.7
      multi_query:
        enabled: true
        provider: helper
        num_variants: 4
      rerank_top_n: 30
      final_top_k: 8
    chunking:
      strategy: recursive
      size: 600
      overlap: 80
    sources:
      - type: file
        path: "{{workspace}}/knowledge"
        extensions: [.md, .txt, .pdf, .html, .csv, .json]
        watch: true
        recursive: true
        max_files: 10000
      - type: database
        connection_id: main_db
        sync:
          strategy: changelog
          auto_create_triggers: true
          interval: 30
        tables:
          customers:
            columns: [id, name, email, company, notes, segment]
            mode: embed_rows
            template: "Client: {name} ({company}, segment {segment}) — {notes}"
          products:
            columns: [id, name, description, category, price]
            mode: embed_rows
            template: "Produit: {name} ({category}, {price}€) — {description}"
          orders:
            mode: schema_only
          revenue:
            mode: schema_only
          support_tickets:
            columns: [id, title, description, status, priority, customer_id]
            mode: embed_rows
            template: "Ticket #{id}: {title} ({status}, {priority}) — {description}"
    auto_index:
      on_start: true
    cache:
      enabled: true
      similarity_threshold: 0.90
      ttl: 1800
      max_entries: 30000
    citations:
      enabled: true
      format: inline
      verify: true
    text2sql:
      enabled: true
      provider: helper
      example_cache: true
    crag:
      enabled: true
      provider: helper
      confidence_threshold: 0.4
      fallback: broader_query

  llm_provider:
    providers:
      helper:
        backend: openai_compat
        model: deepseek-chat
        config:
          api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
          base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"

agents:
  # ── Coordinateur ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: coordinator
    role: coordinator
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      backend: openai_compat
      model: deepseek-chat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      temperature: 0.2
      context:
        max_tokens: 128000
        strategy: summarize
        keep_recent: 15
    modules: [memory]
    system_prompt: |
      Tu es le coordinateur d'une équipe d'agents spécialisés.

      **Tes spécialistes :**
      - `researcher` : Recherche dans les documents et données (RAG hybride + CRAG)
      - `analyst` : Analyse de données et requêtes SQL (Text2SQL)
      - `writer` : Rédaction de synthèses avec citations vérifiées

      **Stratégie :**
      1. Analyse la demande de l'utilisateur
      2. Délègue au(x) bon(s) spécialiste(s)
      3. Synthétise les résultats

      Questions factuelles → researcher
      Questions analytiques (combien, pourcentage, tendance) → analyst
      Demande de rapport/synthèse → researcher PUIS writer
      Questions complexes → researcher ET analyst en parallèle, puis writer

  # ── Chercheur ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: researcher
    role: specialist
    specialty: "Recherche documentaire et données"
    modules: [rag, filesystem]
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      backend: openai_compat
      model: deepseek-chat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      temperature: 0.1
    system_prompt: |
      Tu es un chercheur expert. Tu utilises le RAG pour trouver
      des informations précises dans les documents et données indexés.

      Outils principaux :
      - rag.query : recherche hybride standard
      - rag.multi_query : recherche élargie (questions complexes)

      Retourne TOUJOURS les sources avec citations [N].
      Si pas de résultat pertinent, dis-le clairement.

  # ── Analyste ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: analyst
    role: specialist
    specialty: "Analyse de données et SQL"
    modules: [rag, database]
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      backend: openai_compat
      model: deepseek-chat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      temperature: 0.0
    system_prompt: |
      Tu es un analyste de données. Tu réponds aux questions analytiques
      en utilisant Text2SQL et les données structurées.

      Outils principaux :
      - rag.sql_query : génère et exécute du SQL depuis une question
      - rag.query : pour chercher des données textuelles (clients, produits)

      Pour les questions analytiques (combien, total, moyenne, tendance),
      utilise TOUJOURS sql_query. Cite la requête SQL utilisée.

  # ── Rédacteur ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - id: writer
    role: specialist
    specialty: "Rédaction de synthèses"
    modules: [rag, filesystem]
    brain:
      provider: deepseek
      backend: openai_compat
      model: deepseek-chat
      config:
        api_key: "{{env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}}"
        base_url: "https://api.deepseek.com/v1"
      temperature: 0.3
    system_prompt: |
      Tu es un rédacteur expert. Tu produis des synthèses claires,
      structurées et sourcées à partir des informations collectées.

      Règles :
      - Structure avec des titres et sous-titres
      - Cite CHAQUE affirmation avec [N]
      - Distingue les faits (sourcés) des analyses (ton jugement)
      - Si demandé, écris le rapport dans un fichier avec filesystem.write

capabilities:
  grant:
    - module: rag
    - module: filesystem
      actions: [read, grep, glob, write]
    - module: database
      actions: [fetch_results, introspect, list_tables, describe]
    - module: memory
  deny:
    - module: rag
      actions: [delete_knowledge_base, migrate_embeddings]
      reason: "Opérations d'administration réservées"

execution:
  mode: conversation
  entry_agent: coordinator
  workspace: "{{workspace}}"
  max_turns: 200
  greeting: |
    Équipe RAG multi-agent prête :
    - Chercheur : documents + données indexées (CRAG)
    - Analyste : requêtes SQL analytiques
    - Rédacteur : synthèses sourcées

    Posez votre question ou demandez un rapport.
